findings.why_it_matters: Underlining is the standard's own notation for a REQUIRED word. The transcription applies it inconsistently: it IS preserved on page 895 (`<u>FUNCTION</u>  <u>HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC</u>  ( argument-1 )`) and page 902 (`<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>INTEGER-PART</u> ( argument-1 )`), but dropped in the general formats on pages 892 (15.41.2), 894 (15.42.2), 897 (15.44.2), 898 (15.45.2), 899 (15.46.2), 900 (15.47.2) and 901 (15.48.2). On these particular pages every word in the format is required, so no legal syntax is made to look illegal and no optional word is made to look required -- the loss is presentational only. Recorded as a document-wide convention inconsistency, not a local semantic defect: the same drop occurs in roughly forty of the fifty section 15 function formats.
findings.suggested_repair: Apply the `<u>...</u>` convention already used at 15.43.2 and 15.49.2 uniformly to the general formats at 15.41.2, 15.42.2, 15.44.2, 15.45.2, 15.46.2, 15.47.2 and 15.48.2 (and, as a separate document-wide sweep, to the remaining section 15 function formats). Also normalize the code-span markup, which varies arbitrarily on these pages: plain text (15.41.2, 15.42.2, 15.44.2, 15.45.2), single backticks (15.46.2, 15.47.2), and a fenced block (15.48.2).
